item.title: 🟠 New Zapscape KVM Flaw Could Let Privileged L1 Guest Code Escape to Linux Hosts
item.description:
Why this matters: Hospitality system impact — check guest-facing services and PMS/POS status.
Zapscape, a new Linux kernel vulnerability, could allow an attacker with kernel privileges inside an L1 guest virtual machine (VM) to escape KVM isolation and execute code on the host. The risk applies when nested virtualization is exposed to untrusted guests. The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-64561 and affects KVM/x86's shadow memory management unit (MMU), which manages shadow page

Source: The Hacker News  |  Severity: Important  |  Age: 6h ago

item.title: 🟠 Cisco Patches 12 SD-WAN and IOS XE Flaws, Including Three 9.8 CVSS Score Bugs
item.description:
Why this matters: Vendor advisory — check installed firmware/software version and patch status.
Cisco has rolled out updates to address multiple critical security vulnerabilities impacting Catalyst SD-WAN and IOS XE Software as part of a comprehensive internal security review.
